Scouting Summary

Common themes

  • Right Fast, averaging 142.3 kph (up to 153.2).
  • Typical length is 6-7m (their good length); median 7.8 m.
  • Stock ball is a good length outside off, seaming away, swinging in, hitting the stumps (26% of deliveries).
  • Round the wicket to LHB 48% · over the wicket to RHB (round 5%).
  • Round the wicket he shifts his pitching line from 6th stump to down leg.
  • Across an over he varies his length a lot, banging it in more as the over goes on.

Biggest threats

  • Most dangerous length is Yorker/Full (3 wkts, 3.9% adjusted strike).
  • Danger pitching line: Wide of 6th (over the wicket).
  • Takes 22% of wickets pitching a good length wide outside off, mostly over the wicket (80%).
  • Beats the bat 9.2% of tracked balls (false-shot 18.2%).
  • Gets you caught behind more than most — 78% of his wickets (1.2× the typical rate for this type).
  • 67% of catches are behind the wicket (keeper / slips / gully); most often to keeper, slip: 1st, slip: 3rd.

Areas to exploit

  • Concedes most runs pitching a good length on the 6th stump (12% of runs).
  • Short ball: 47% of deliveries, economy 3.5 — 32 wkts from 1425 short balls.
  • Away from yorker/full, the wicket threat drops off — look to score in the less-productive lengths.
  • Most of his runs leak square/through the off side (52%) — his main scoring release.
  • Cash in when he goes back of a length wide outside off (economy 4.1, beats the bat only 19%).

Solid line = career, dotted = last 3 years (where enough recent balls). Percentile within same-type peers (grey = the peer distribution, line = this bowler). Release/crease vs hand × pace/spin; movement/speed/repeatability vs pace/spin. Release & speed are modern-era (2017+ / partial). Crease variation = how much he moves his release point sideways across the crease from ball to ball (within his main angle): a high percentile = he varies where he lets the ball go a lot, a low percentile = he releases from the same spot every ball. Repeatability = length consistency over his stock-length band (2–11 m, so deliberate yorkers and bouncers don't count as poor control): a high percentile = tighter, more metronomic lengths than peers; a low percentile = he varies his length more. A marker at the very edge = he sits beyond the typical peer range on that trait.

Sequencing & Over Construction

Variable with his length (length spread ±2.3 m; more repeatable than 29% of pace bowlers); tends to bang it in later in the over (short 11%→23% by the 5th–6th ball); and holds the same crease position through the over.
Doubles up on the short ball — pitches up only 32% of the time after banging one in.
Across 58 dismissals, his wicket ball is close in length and pace to the delivery before it — he builds pressure with repetition, not a big change-up.
